subject: biology
title: The water cycle and potable water
key_idea: The water cycle moves water between the sea, the air and the land. It supplies fresh water to plants and animals on land. In places with too little fresh water, **potable** (safe to drink) water can be made from seawater by **desalination**.

blocks.text: Water is continuously evaporated and precipitated. This section covers the processes in the cycle and why living things depend on it.

items.meaning: Liquid water changing into water vapour, mainly from the sea, lakes and soil.
Water vapour lost from the leaves of plants.
Water vapour cooling and changing into tiny droplets of liquid water, forming clouds.
Water falling from the clouds to the ground as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Water flowing over the land into streams, rivers, lakes and the sea.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of the water cycle in order, starting with water evaporating from the sea and ending with water flowing back to the sea.
diagram.prompt: Put the water cycle in the correct order
steps: Water evaporates from the sea, lakes and soil, and plants lose water vapour by transpiration
The water vapour rises and cools
The water vapour condenses to form clouds
Water falls as precipitation, such as rain or snow
Water runs off the land into rivers and lakes, or soaks into the soil, and drains back to the sea

items: Water is continuously evaporated and precipitated.
Evaporation and transpiration lift water into the air. Condensation forms clouds. Precipitation brings it back down.

sections.heading: Why the water cycle matters to living things

blocks.text: All living things need water. The water cycle provides fresh water for plants and animals on land before it drains into the seas.

items: Plants take in water through their roots from the soil, which rain has refilled.
Animals drink fresh water from rivers, lakes and puddles.
Rain and run-off keep rivers and lakes full, so the organisms that live in them do not dry out.
Run-off can wash minerals into lakes and rivers.
Without precipitation, soil dries out and land can turn to desert.
The water cycle supplies fresh water to organisms on land.
If the supply of fresh water falls, plants and animals suffer.

blocks.text: Potable water is safe to drink. In places with a drought, or too little fresh water, it can be made from seawater.

items.meaning: Water that is safe to drink.
Removing the salt from seawater to make fresh water.

items: River water is **filtered** to remove solids such as debris.
It is then treated with chemicals, such as chlorine, to destroy **pathogens**.

diagram.alt: Desalination: seawater is heated, the water evaporates leaving the salt behind, the water vapour condenses, and the fresh water is collected.
steps: The water evaporates, leaving the salt behind
The water vapour is cooled and condenses

items: Fresh water is filtered to remove solids, then treated with chemicals to destroy pathogens.
Desalination makes potable water from seawater: evaporate, condense and collect.

checks.q: Name the process by which water vapour changes into liquid droplets to form clouds.
Explain why the water cycle is important to organisms living on land.
checks.a: It provides fresh water, as rain, for plants and animals on land before the water drains into the seas. Plants take it in from the soil and animals drink it.

checks.q: Describe how seawater can be turned into drinking water.
checks.a: Desalination: heat the seawater so the water evaporates and the salt is left behind, then condense the water vapour and collect the liquid water.

exam_phrases: climate change has increased the area of deserts
more water is used to grow crops
the water cycle provides water for plants and animals on land before the water goes into lakes and seas

mistakes.wrong: More people have a water shortage because each person drinks less water, or because some countries have built de-salting factories.
mistakes.right: Neither is credited. The causes credited are that climate change has increased the area of deserts and that more water is used to grow crops.

mistakes.wrong: There were 270 000 000 people with a severe water shortage.
mistakes.right: The question asks for standard form. The final mark is for 2.7 × 10⁸.

worked_example.question:
The water cycle provides water for plants and animals on land before the water goes into lakes and seas.

In 2007 the population of the world was 6 000 000 000. A study found that 4.5% of the population had severe water shortage.

Calculate how many people had severe water shortage.

Give your answer in standard form.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the method, one for 270 000 000 and one for standard form. A wrong number written correctly in standard form still earns the final mark.

exam_phrases: desalination / remove salt from the water

mistakes.wrong: Water is filtered to kill pathogens.
mistakes.right: Filtering removes objects or debris. Chemicals are used to destroy pathogens.

mistakes.wrong: Seawater is turned into drinking water by removing the salt.
mistakes.right: This gives one mark at most. A description needs two points from: remove the salt (desalination), evaporate the water, and condense the vapour and collect it.

worked_example.question:
The Canary Islands do not have enough fresh water.

Describe how seawater can be turned into drinking water.
answer_points: Desalination removes the salt from the water.
The water is heated so it evaporates.
The water vapour is condensed and collected.
worked_example.tip: Two of the three points score. Distillation is accepted for both the evaporate and condense points.

exam_phrases: provides organisms with enough water to live in

mistakes.wrong: Run-off gives the organisms more water.
mistakes.right: "More water" is ignored. Say that it replenishes the lake so it does not dry out, or that it provides enough water for the organisms to live in.

mistakes.wrong: Run-off brings nutrients into the lake.
mistakes.right: "Nutrients" is ignored. Write minerals, or name a mineral.

worked_example.question:
The water cycle takes place around a lake. Surface run-off water passes through soil and back into the lake.

Write down one reason why surface run-off water is important to organisms living in the lake.
answer_points: It prevents the lake drying out, or replenishes the lake water.
Or: it washes minerals into the lake.
worked_example.tip: Any one of these scores the mark.
